notes: All figures from TSMC's FY2024 Form 20-F (fiscal year ended 31 December 2024) and 2024 Annual Report, both downloaded from investor.tsmc.com (the site sits behind a Cloudflare check, so the PDFs were fetched through a real browser session on that domain). Amounts are NT$ (ISO TWD) millions converted to billions. FOUNDER: Morris Chang retired in 2018. His name does not appear anywhere in the 20-F (Item 6 directors/officers and Item 7 major shareholders were checked) and appears in the English annual report only in narrative references to 'TSMC's Founder, Dr. Morris Chang' (governance and ESG sections), not in any shareholding table. The Chinese-language 2024 annual report (https://investor.tsmc.com/sites/ir/annual-report/2024/2024-Annual%20Report-C.pdf) was also checked: 張忠謀 appears only twice, both in the same narrative passages. Status is therefore no-reported-stake. HOLDERS: the National Development Fund (6.38%) is the only 5%+ holder in the 20-F. The annual report's top-ten list (record date 18 December 2024, the Q2 2024 dividend record date) is led by 'ADR-Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd.' at 20.49%; that is the ADS depositary (Citibank, N.A.'s nominee), not a beneficial owner, so it is omitted. The Government of Singapore (2.63%) and Norges Bank (1.78%) lines are held through Citibank (Taiwan) as custodian, but the beneficial owner is named in the filing. Their percentages are at an earlier date (18 December 2024) than the NDF figure (28 February 2025). BUYBACKS: the 2024 buyback of 3,249,000 shares (about NT$3,089 million) was made by TSMC itself and the shares were cancelled on 1 September 2024. The 20-F (Item 16E) says its purpose was 'to offset the dilutive effect of the issuance of RSAs under our equity incentive plans'. It is included as a company repurchase, not an employee-trust purchase. DIVIDENDS: cash-flow line 'Cash dividends' (NT$363,055.2 million paid in 2024). This differs from the NT$414,915.5 million declared in the equity statement because quarterly dividends are paid about six months after approval. The cash-flow statement shows no separate dividend line for non-controlling interests. STOCK COMP: equity-settled share-based compensation (NT$1,242.7 million, cash-flow add-back). The employee-benefits note also lists NT$403.5 million of cash-settled share-based payments, for NT$1,646.2 million in total; the cash-settled part is paid in cash, not stock, and is excluded. TSMC's much larger employee profit-sharing bonuses are cash and are not counted here. GEOGRAPHY: from the notes to the financial statements, by customer headquarters country. Item 5 of the 20-F gives an alternative split (North America 2,031,326; China 331,673; Asia Pacific 284,308; EMEA 102,761; Japan 144,240, NT$ millions), which is not used.

footprint.notes: All figures are from the 2024 Form 20-F on sec.gov (TSMC's own sites block scripted fetches). Employees: Item 6.D table of full-time employees by location, Dec 31, 2024; the six Taiwan locations are recorded as regions (countries ["TW"]) because the table has no Taiwan total, and none was summed. North America and Europe are the table's own groupings (no country list). Fabs: the 20-F gives fab counts in words ("nine of our fabs are located in the Hsinchu Science Park, two fabs are located in the Central Taiwan Science Park, five fabs are located in the Southern Taiwan Science Park, two fabs are located in the United States, one fab is located in Shanghai, one fab is located in Nanjing, and one fab is located in Japan"); quotes carry a bracketed [nine = 9] style annotation. These counts include advanced backend fabs. The fab sentence's science-park areas may not match the employee table's rows of the same name (it puts no fab in Taoyuan City or Miaoli County, where the table shows 2,817 and 3,055 employees), so a row's fab count and employee count may not describe exactly the same area. Shanghai and Nanjing (one fab each) are shown as sites, not summed into a China fab count. No U.S. state rows: the U.S. fabs are one in Washington State (Fab 11) and one in Arizona (Fab 21), shown as sites with state codes; no per-state employee or investment figures are published in the 20-F. Fab 22 (Kaohsiung) and Fab 24 (Dresden) were not yet operating. Site descriptions take year/wafer size/technology from the 20-F fab table (as of Feb 28, 2025; technology as of 2024 year-end).
